newsitem.title: USA: Dow off highs as bonds shave gains at midday.
newsitem.headline: Dow off highs as bonds shave gains at midday.

text.p: The Dow Industrials were off their highs at midday, taking their cue from bonds which cut their gains after an early rally.
The market benefitted from favorable testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and Intel Corp's report that first quarter price increases on microprocessors would be lower than expected.
The Industrials were up 16 to 6757 while gainers led losers by 13 to nine. The long bond was up 5/32 to yield 6.90 percent.

"The bonds call the market. When bonds falter, stocks follow suit," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. He did not attribute the drop in bonds to any aspect of Greenspan's testimony, which analysts said was favorable for the bond market.

"Most of his comments can be taken as positive," one analyst said. "Technically, the bond market has not been behaving too well," one analyst said. "The bonds tick up, but they can't hold their gains."
Analysts also said the bond market was turning cautious ahead of Friday's fourth quarter real GDP.

In prepared testimony before the Senate Finance Committee, Greenspan said there is a very high probability that the consumer price index, a leading gauge of inflation, was overstating inflation by 0.5 to 1.5 percentage points a year.
He also said that he opposed the idea of the United States government becoming a huge stakeholder in common stocks through the Social Security System.

Intel was up 2-3/4 at 157-1/2, bolstering semiconductors and other high techs. The Nasdaq Composite, heavily weighted with high techs, was up six at 1361. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Semiconductor Index was up eight points at 279.

"I think the high tech universe is still one where stock selection is quite important," said Marshall Accuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney. "I would go with the big ones, the ones with the real potential for growth.
"I think that Intel will be a $200 stock by the end of the year, but I'm not sure I can make such a statement for any of the others."
Elsewhere, defensive issues benefitted from several day's worth of softer than expected economic data.
Dow component Merck & Co Inc was up one at 89-1/4. Bristol-Myers Squibb Co was up 1-5/8 at 124-7/8, Philip Morris Cos Inc was up 1-3/4 at 118-1/8.
Wachtel said that money managers were running out of impetus to push the market higher.
"Fourth quarter earnings are coming to an end, the flow of money into mutual funds will slow in February and we are going to have an FOMC meeting," he said.
"We corrected 225 points over five days and then we rebounded 80 points without a corresponding move in the broad market. We can't go up every day in every way."
Among today's special situations, shares of Doncasters Plc DCS.N were up 3-1/2 at 20 in heavy trading on the NYSE as the company went public after its spinoff by Canadian mining company Inco Ltd.
